pin_variations.title: Healthy Basil Chicken Recipe for Volume Eating and High Protein Gains
pin_variations.description: Want a giant bowl of flavor without the calories? This slow cooker basil chicken is packed with protein and herbs for volume eating that satisfies. Try it today and feel full the right way! 🌿🍴 #VolumeEating #HighProteinSnack #LowCalorie

ingredients: 1.5 lbs boneless skinless chicken breasts, raw
1 tsp olive oil (optional, minimal fat for texture)
1/4 tsp xanthan gum (optional, for thickening sauce without calories)
yield: Approximately 6 servings, about 1 cup cooked chicken per serving, perfect for meal prep containers
introduction: I’ve always struggled with feeling hungry on low-calorie diets, especially when trying to get enough protein without sacrificing volume. That’s why I fell in love with this slow cooker basil chicken recipe. It’s one of those dishes that fills your plate and your stomach without blowing your calorie budget. Unlike store-bought protein bars or pre-packaged meals that leave me wanting more, this recipe delivers a hearty portion of tender chicken infused with fresh basil and garlic, all cooked low and slow for maximum flavor. The trick I use to keep the sauce silky without adding calories is a pinch of xanthan gum, which thickens the broth beautifully and keeps everything luscious. Plus, using chicken breasts keeps the protein count high and fat low, perfect for cutting or meal prep days. I’ve made this recipe dozens of times, once even accidentally overcooking it but still ending up with juicy, shreddable chicken that my family devoured. It’s incredibly forgiving and super easy to throw together before work or on a lazy Sunday. You’ll get about 6 generous servings that store well in the fridge, and it’s fantastic paired with steamed veggies or over a bed of cauliflower rice. I usually eat this for dinner or pack it as a post-workout meal to keep my energy up without feeling weighed down. The fresh basil brightens the dish and makes it feel special, even though it’s so simple. If you want a high-protein, low-calorie meal that actually fills you up and tastes amazing, this basil chicken is a winner in my book.

instructions.instruction: Place the raw chicken breasts into the slow cooker. Pour in the chicken broth, making sure the chicken is mostly submerged to keep it moist during cooking. Add minced garlic, lemon juice, dried oregano, salt, and pepper. The broth acts as a cooking medium that infuses flavor and keeps the chicken juicy without adding fat. Avoid overfilling the slow cooker as this can dilute the flavors. The liquid also helps prevent the chicken from drying out during the long cooking time.
instructions.doneness_cue: Chicken breasts are fully covered or mostly covered in broth and seasonings are evenly distributed.

instructions.instruction: Sprinkle the chopped fresh basil over the chicken and stir gently to distribute. Fresh basil adds a bright, herbal note that elevates the dish without calories. Adding it at the start ensures the flavor infuses into the chicken as it cooks. Avoid adding basil too late or it won’t impart its full aroma. If using xanthan gum, mix it with a small amount of cold broth or water before adding to avoid clumps.
instructions.doneness_cue: Basil is evenly scattered and incorporated, with no clumps of xanthan gum visible if used.

instructions.instruction: Cover and cook on low for 4 hours or on high for 2-3 hours. Slow cooking allows the chicken to absorb the basil and garlic flavors fully while becoming tender without drying out. Resist the urge to open the lid frequently, as this releases heat and extends cooking time. The low temperature breaks down muscle fibers gently, resulting in juicy chicken perfect for shredding or slicing.
instructions.doneness_cue: Chicken is opaque and easily shredded with a fork.

instructions.instruction: Once cooked, remove the chicken breasts and place them on a cutting board. Use two forks to shred the chicken finely. Shredding increases surface area, helping the meat absorb any remaining sauce when returned to the slow cooker. This also makes the portion feel larger, which is great for volume eating.
instructions.doneness_cue: Chicken shreds easily without resistance and looks moist.

instructions.instruction: If you want a thicker sauce, stir the xanthan gum slurry into the broth in the slow cooker now. Mix well and let it sit on warm heat for 5-10 minutes to thicken. Xanthan gum is a zero-calorie thickener that creates a creamy texture without fat. Don’t add too much or the sauce will become gummy. Stir gently to avoid lumps.
instructions.doneness_cue: Sauce coats the back of a spoon and has a smooth, slightly thickened consistency.

instructions.instruction: Return the shredded chicken to the thickened sauce and stir to combine. This step ensures every bite is juicy and flavorful. The sauce clings to the meat, enhancing mouthfeel and satiety without adding calories or fat.
instructions.doneness_cue: Chicken is evenly coated with sauce and looks glossy but not watery.

instructions.instruction: Taste and adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed. Brightening with lemon juice at the end balances the basil’s herbal notes and lifts the flavors. Don’t skip this step, as it makes the dish pop without extra calories.
instructions.doneness_cue: Balanced flavor with a fresh, slightly tangy finish.

instructions.instruction: Serve immediately over steamed vegetables, cauliflower rice, or store in airtight containers for meal prep. Portion control is easy since each serving has a consistent protein count and low calories. The large volume of chicken and sauce helps keep you full longer.
instructions.doneness_cue: Dish plated attractively with visible basil and moist chicken.

instructions.instruction: For meal prep, cool the chicken completely before refrigerating. This prevents condensation and preserves texture. Reheat gently in the microwave or on the stovetop with a splash of broth to maintain moisture. Avoid overheating which can dry out the chicken.
instructions.doneness_cue: Reheated chicken is warm, moist, and flavorful without drying.

why_this_recipe_works.section: Why This Slow Cooker Basil Chicken Fills You Up Without Extra Calories
why_this_recipe_works.content:
This slow cooker basil chicken recipe leverages the power of protein to keep you full longer while staying low calorie. Protein has a high thermic effect of food (TEF), meaning your body burns more calories digesting it compared to fats or carbs. That alone helps support fat loss and satiety. But beyond that, the recipe combines protein with high-volume, low-calorie ingredients like broth and fresh basil to stretch the portion size without adding calories. This volume eating technique physically fills your stomach, triggering fullness signals to your brain.

Using chicken breast provides a lean protein source that’s easy to digest and low in fat, which is key for keeping calories down. The slow cooking method breaks down tough fibers gently, making the chicken tender and juicy, so you don’t feel deprived of texture or flavor. Incorporating fresh basil and lemon juice adds bright, fresh flavors without sugar or fat, making the dish taste satisfying and complex.

The xanthan gum is a clever addition that mimics creaminess without adding fat or calories. It thickens the broth into a luscious sauce that clings to the chicken, creating a rich mouthfeel that tricks your brain into thinking you’re eating something indulgent. This is crucial because fat typically provides that texture, but here we rely on hydrocolloids to achieve similar effects while keeping the recipe lean.

Finally, the large portion size and moist texture help combat the psychological challenge of dieting – you see a big plate of food and feel satisfied visually and physically. This recipe hits all the right notes: high protein, low calorie, volume eating, and delicious flavor, making it a perfect staple for anyone wanting to eat well while cutting calories.

ingredient_notes.boneless skinless chicken breasts: Look for fresh or thawed chicken breasts with minimal added solutions or marinades to keep calories low. Chicken breast is ideal for low-calorie high-protein recipes because it has about 31 grams of protein per 100 grams with very little fat. Avoid pre-seasoned or breaded varieties as they add hidden calories. In this recipe, the chicken is slow-cooked to retain moisture and tenderness without needing fat.
ingredient_notes.fresh basil leaves: Fresh basil adds aromatic flavor without calories or sodium. When buying, choose vibrant green leaves with no signs of wilting or browning. Dried basil can be used but fresh gives a brighter, more complex flavor. Basil’s essential oils also enhance satiety by making the dish more satisfying to eat.
ingredient_notes.chicken broth low sodium: Using low-sodium broth controls salt intake while providing moisture and flavor. Broth adds volume and moisture to the dish, helping keep the chicken juicy during slow cooking. Check labels to avoid added sugars or fillers that increase calories. Homemade broth is best if you want full control.
ingredient_notes.xanthan gum: Xanthan gum is a zero-calorie thickener that mimics creaminess in low-fat recipes. It’s a polysaccharide that absorbs water and forms a gel, giving sauces a silky texture without fat. Use sparingly (about 1/4 tsp) to avoid gummy texture. It’s a great tool for making low-calorie protein dishes feel indulgent without added calories.
ingredient_notes.lemon juice fresh: Fresh lemon juice brightens and balances flavors with its acidity. It contains virtually no calories and helps enhance the herbal notes of basil. Use freshly squeezed juice rather than bottled for best flavor. Adding lemon juice at the end preserves its fresh aroma.

pro_tips.tip: Add xanthan gum slowly and mix thoroughly to avoid lumps.
pro_tips.reason: Xanthan gum can clump if added directly to warm liquids. Mixing it first with a small amount of cold liquid creates a slurry that disperses evenly when added to the hot broth. This ensures a smooth, creamy sauce without unpleasant texture.

pro_tips.tip: Don’t skip the lemon juice at the end.
pro_tips.reason: The acidity brightens the basil and garlic flavors, making the dish taste fresher and more vibrant. Without it, the chicken can taste flat or dull, especially since the recipe avoids added fats or sugars.

pro_tips.tip: Use slow cooker low setting for best texture.
pro_tips.reason: Cooking on low breaks down the chicken fibers gently, resulting in tender, juicy meat. High heat can dry out chicken breasts quickly, making them tough and less enjoyable.

common_mistakes_to_avoid.mistake: Skipping the thickener and ending with watery sauce.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.why_it_happens: Many expect broth to reduce in the slow cooker, but it often stays watery due to the sealed environment. Without thickening, the sauce can feel thin and less satisfying.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.fix: Use a small amount of xanthan gum or cornstarch slurry after cooking to thicken the sauce. This adds creaminess without calories or fat.

common_mistakes_to_avoid.mistake: Using full-fat chicken or pre-marinated cuts.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.why_it_happens: Pre-packaged chicken often contains added oils or marinades that increase calories unknowingly.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.fix: Choose plain, boneless skinless chicken breasts to control fat and calories precisely.

variations.name: Spicy Basil Chicken
variations.description: Add red pepper flakes or chopped fresh chili to the slow cooker for a spicy kick. This variation adds a metabolism-boosting element without extra calories. Expect a bolder flavor profile with the same tender texture and protein content.
variations.technical_note: Add spices at the start with broth to infuse heat evenly. Adjust spice level to taste.

variations.name: Basil Chicken with Mushrooms
variations.description: Include sliced mushrooms in the slow cooker for added volume and umami flavor. Mushrooms are low calorie and high in fiber, complementing the protein-rich chicken perfectly. This adds a meaty texture without fat.
variations.technical_note: Add mushrooms at the beginning to cook down and blend flavors.

storage_and_reheating.room_temperature: This chicken should not be left at room temperature for more than 2 hours due to the risk of bacterial growth, especially since it contains cooked poultry and broth. Always cover it tightly if left out briefly.
storage_and_reheating.refrigerator: Store in airtight containers for up to 4 days. The flavor deepens after a day, and the sauce thickens slightly. Reheat gently with a splash of broth to restore moisture. The chicken holds its texture well when chilled.
storage_and_reheating.freezer: Freeze in meal prep containers for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating. Texture may be slightly less tender after freezing but still delicious.
storage_and_reheating.reheating: Reheat in the microwave or stovetop over low heat with a splash of broth to prevent drying. Avoid overheating as it can toughen the chicken.
storage_and_reheating.make_ahead_strategy: Prepare the chicken and sauce fully, shred, and store in containers. Add fresh basil or lemon juice just before serving to keep brightness. Perfect for meal prep Sundays.

faq.question: Can I use chicken thighs instead of breasts?
faq.answer: Yes, chicken thighs will work and add a bit more fat and flavor. Adjust cooking time slightly if thighs are bone-in. Thighs are juicier but higher in calories, so factor that into your macros.

faq.question: What if I don’t have xanthan gum?
faq.answer: You can skip it or use a small amount of cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce. Without a thickener, the sauce will be more broth-like but still tasty.

faq.question: Can I make this in an Instant Pot instead of a slow cooker?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Use the poultry setting or cook on high pressure for about 10-12 minutes, then natural release. You may want to thicken the sauce afterward on sauté mode.

faq.question: How do I avoid the chicken drying out?
faq.answer: Make sure the chicken is mostly submerged in broth and cook on low heat. Also, don’t overcook; check for doneness at the 4-hour mark.

faq.question: Is this recipe suitable for cutting or weight loss?
faq.answer: Yes, it’s lean, high protein, and low calorie, making it ideal for cutting phases or anyone wanting to lose weight without hunger.

faq.question: Can I freeze leftovers?
faq.answer: Yes, freezing up to 3 months is fine. Thaw in the fridge overnight and reheat gently to maintain texture.

faq.question: What sides go well with this chicken?
faq.answer: Steamed veggies, cauliflower rice, or a simple salad are great low-calorie, high-volume sides that keep the meal balanced.

faq.question: How do I prevent the sauce from tasting bland?
faq.answer: Use fresh basil and lemon juice, and season well with salt and pepper. These brighten flavors without adding calories.

conclusion: Give this slow cooker basil chicken a try and enjoy a delicious, filling high-protein meal that fits your low-calorie goals. I’d love to hear how it works for your meal prep or cutting phase!
